Sample rows of a dataset

Source: R/read.R
store_sample.Rd

Reads a random sample of about n rows without reading the whole dataset. Row groups (blocks of rows inside the files) are picked at random across files, with probability proportional to their rows, and only those are read; the filters are applied, and n rows are drawn from the rows found. When the filters leave fewer than n rows, further row groups are read until n rows are found or the dataset is exhausted.

Usage

store_sample(
  st,
  dataset,
  n = 1000,
  ...,
  columns = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  geometry = TRUE,
  version = NULL
)

Arguments

st

A store connection made by store_connect().

dataset

Name of the dataset: the full name, or its last part when that is unique in the store.

n

Number of rows wanted.

...

Filter expressions, as in dplyr::filter().

columns

Columns to return, as in dplyr::select() (tidyselect); NULL for all. The geometry column is controlled by geometry. A raster has no column selection.

seed

NULL, or a number that makes the sample reproducible. The global random stream is left as it was (withr::with_seed()).

geometry

FALSE drops the geometry before reading and returns a tibble.

version

NULL for the current version, or the 16 hex characters of an earlier version kept in the history.

Value

A tibble, or an sf object for geospatial data read with geometry, with at most n rows.

Details

This is a cluster sample, not a simple random sample: rows are stored sorted (by key, or spatially by H3 cell), so the rows of one row group are alike, and the sample covers only as many clusters as row groups were read. Use it to look at data, not to estimate.

Unlike store_read(), it never copies the dataset to a secondary location.

See also

store_read().

Examples

location <- file.path(tempdir(), "rcs-example-sample")
st <- store_connect(location, create = TRUE)
store_write(st, rcs_sim_table(2000), "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales", description = "Simulated daily sales.",
  key = c("shop_id", "date", "product"), partition = "year"
)
#> ℹ Writing "sales/daily": 2,000 rows in 2 files (partition year).
#> ✔ primary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sample  2/2
#>   files sent  89.1 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 1 location. Catalogs updated.
store_sample(st, "sales/daily", n = 5, qty > 10, seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 15
#>   shop_id date        year product   qty price promo grade delivered      big
#>     <int> <date>     <int> <fct>   <int> <dbl> <lgl> <ord> <date>     <int64>
#> 1       3 2024-04-22  2024 p14        28  95.5 FALSE high  2024-04-28   9 e15
#> 2       5 2024-05-16  2024 p10        23 198.  FALSE low   2024-05-18   9 e15
#> 3       5 2024-06-16  2024 p02        19  20.0 FALSE mid   2024-06-22   9 e15
#> 4       7 2024-07-02  2024 p15        27 164.  FALSE low   2024-07-10   3.e 2
#> 5       9 2024-09-10  2024 p16        15 123.  FALSE high  2024-09-15   9 e15
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: wait <drtn>, note <chr>, tags <list>, ts <dttm>,
#> #   ts_local <dttm>
unlink(location, recursive = TRUE)
